findings.title: Bound scans before they enter the cleanup reserve
findings.originalText: Fresh evidence in the corrected head shows that `probe_timeout()` only bounds subprocess probes; it does not bound the synchronous filesystem work that follows a successful check. For example, `monitor()` enters `resources()` and `projection_guard()` after checking this deadline, and those functions recursively scan/hash the projection and external caches without rechecking it. If one of those scans starts just before `work_deadline` on a slow or stalled external volume, it can cross the reserved 150 seconds while Unity is still live, so `closure()` again starts with insufficient TERM/restoration time. Add deadline checks within the long scans or reserve a bounded worst-case allowance before entering them.

findings.title: Reserve time for final evidence and receipt emission
findings.originalText: This formula reserves exactly 90 seconds for closure and 60 seconds for restoration, but no time for the mandatory work after restoration. When T and cleanup consume their full allocations, `restore_all()` can finish at `execution_deadline`; `main()` then still writes `compile.json`, `after.json`, `process-after.json`, hashes every evidence file, and writes `receipt.json` without another deadline check. The run therefore exceeds the unchanged 900-second cap while retaining `TEST_PASS`, and `mechanicalExecutionSeconds` is evaluated before the evidence hashing and receipt write, so the receipt also underreports the overrun. Reserve finalization time inside the cap or make exceeding the deadline fail the run.
